svg.title: CJC-1295 and ipamorelin: 28 years, no trial of the stack
svg.desc: Timeline. 1998, Novo Nordisk describes ipamorelin in rats and pigs. 2002, ConjuChem files its patent on CJC-1295, with the peptide without DAC tested only as a short-lived control in rats. 2006, CJC-1295 with DAC tested in 63 healthy adults; an HIV trial is stopped after a patient dies of a heart attack. 2009, Norwegian police seize CJC-1295 without DAC. 2010, FDA approves tesamorelin (Egrifta) and ConjuChem files for bankruptcy. 2014, a failed ipamorelin surgery trial is published and a 320-patient trial ends, never reported. 2023, FDA puts ipamorelin on its compounding risk list for outsourcing facilities. 2024, FDA advisers vote ipamorelin 0 to 12 and CJC-1295 0 to 13 (one form 1 to 12). 2026, neither is on FDA’s next advisory agendas while a peptide policy sits at the White House.
